questions.problem: In a hardware store, there are three boxes containing light bulbs. Box $A$ contains $15$ bulbs, of which $2$ are defective. Box $B$ contains $10$ bulbs, of which $1$ is defective. And box $C$ contains $10$ light bulbs, of which $2$ are defective. A box is selected at random, and a bulb is randomly selected from the box. Find the probability that the bulb is defective.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event of selecting a defective bulb, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the bulb is from box $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the bulb is from box $B$

- let $C$ be the event that the bulb is from box $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space. 

To calculate the probability of selecting a defective bulb at random from one of the three boxes, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a box is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $2$ defective bulbs out of $15$  in box $A,$ $1$ defective bulb out of $10$ in box $B,$ and $2$  defective bulbs out of $10$ bulbs in box $C,$ we have 

$$
P(D|A)=\frac{2}{15},\,P(D|B)=\frac{1}{10},\,P(D|C)=\frac{2}{10}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a defective bulb at random from one of the three boxes is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\  & =(\frac{2}{15})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{1}{10})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{2}{10})(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{45}+\frac{1}{30}+\frac{2}{30} \\  & =\frac{13}{90}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A company produces replacement batteries for a particular cell phone model at three locations. Location $A$ produces $30%$ of the batteries, of which $3%$ are defective. Location $B$ produces $38%$ of the batteries, of which $5%$ are defective. And location $C$  produces $32%$ of the batteries, of which also $5%$ are defective. What is the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that the battery is defective, and

- let $A$ be the event that the battery was produced at location $A,$

- let $B$  be the event that the battery was produced at location $B,$

- let $C$  be the event that the battery was produced at location $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since  location $A$ produces $30%$ of the batteries,  location $B$ produces $38%$ of the batteries, and location $C$ produces $32%$ of the batteries, we have

$$
P(A)=0.3,\,P(B)=0.38,\,P(C)=0.32.
$$

- Since $3%$ of the batteries produced at location $A$, $5%$ of the batteries produced at location $B$, and $5%$ of the batteries produced at  location $C,$ are defective, we have 

$$
P(D|A)=0.03,\,P(D|B)=0.05,\,P(D|C)=0.05.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\  & =(0.03)(0.3)+(0.05)(0.38)+(0.05)(0.32) \\  & =0.009+0.019+0.016 \\  & =0.044.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: In a gas station, $40%$ of the clients buy Regular gasoline, $45%$ buy Premium gasoline, and $15%$ buy Supreme gasoline. If $65%$ of the clients that purchase Regular gasoline paid with a credit card, $50%$ of the clients that buy Premium gasoline paid with a credit card, and $60%$ of the clients that buy Supreme gasoline paid with a credit card,  what is the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card?
questions.worked_solution:
Let  $C$ be the event that the client paid with a credit card, and

- let $R$ be the event that the client bought Regular gasoline,

- let $Q$  be the event that the client bought Premium gasoline,

- let $S$ be the event that the client bought Supreme gasoline.

Then the disjoint union $R⊔Q⊔S$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(C) & =P(C\cap R)+P(C\cap Q)+P(C\cap S) \\  & =P(C|R)P(R)+P(C|Q)P(Q)+P(C|S)P(S)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $40%$ of the clients buy Regular gasoline, $45%$ of the clients buy Premium gasoline, and $15%$ of the clients buy Supreme gasoline, we have

$$
P(R)=0.4,\,P(Q)=0.45,\,P(S)=0.15.
$$

- Since $65%$ of the clients that buy Regular gasoline, $50%$ of the clients that buy Premium gasoline, and $60%$ of the clients that buy Supreme gasoline,  paid with a credit card, we have

$$
P(C|R)=0.65,\,P(C|Q)=0.5,\,P(C|S)=0.6.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(C) & =P(C|R)P(R)+P(C|Q)P(Q)+P(C|S)P(S) \\  & =(0.65)(0.4)+(0.5)(0.45)+(0.6)(0.15) \\  & =0.26+0.225+0.009 \\  & =0.575.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A company manufactures electronic components. Of the component population, $45%$ are produced by machine $A,$  $25%$ by machine $B,$ and $30%$ by machine $C.$ If $5%$ of the components produced by machine $A$ and $3%$ of those produced by machine $B$ are defective, and the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is $0.042,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected component produced by machine $C$ is defective?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a randomly selected component is defective, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected component is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation. 

- Since machine $A$ produces $45%$ of the components, machine $B$ produces $25%$ of the components, and machine $C$ produces $30%$ of the components, we have

$$
P(A)=0.45,\,P(B)=0.25,\,P(C)=0.3.
$$

- Since $5%$ of the components produced by machine $A$ and $3%$ of the components produced by machine $B$ are defective, we have

$$
P(D|A)=0.05,\,P(D|B)=0.03
$$

- Since the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is $0.042,$ we have

$$
P(D)=0.042.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(D|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\ 0.042 & =(0.05)(0.45)+(0.03)(0.25)+P(D|C)(0.3) \\ 0.042 & =0.0225+0.0075+0.3P(D|C) \\ 0.3P(D|C) & =0.012 \\ P(D|C) & =0.04\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected component produced by machine $C$ is defective is $0.04.$

questions.problem: A cattle rancher has three ranches, where $34%$ of the rancher's cows are on ranch $A$, $36%$ are on ranch $B,$ and $30%$ on ranch $C.$ If $25%$ of all cows on ranch $A$ and $20%$ of all cows on ranch $B$ are dairy cows, and the probability that a randomly selected cow from any of the three ranches is a dairy cow is $37%,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected cow from ranch $C$ is a dairy cow?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a selected cow is a dairy cow, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $A$,

- let $B$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $B$,

- let $C$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that the randomly selected cow is a dairy cow, we use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation. 

- Since $34%$ of all the rancher's cows are on ranch $A$, $36%$ are on ranch $B,$ and $30%$ are on ranch $C,$ we have

$$
P(A)=0.34,\,P(B)=0.36,\,P(C)=0.3.
$$

- Since $25%$ of all cows on ranch $A$ and $20%$ of all cows on ranch $B$ are dairy cows, we have 

$$
P(D|A)=0.25,\,P(D|B)=0.2.
$$

- Since the probability that a randomly selected cow from any of the three ranches is  a dairy cow is $37%,$ we have

$$
P(D)=0.37.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(D|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\ 0.37 & =(0.25)(0.34)+(0.2)(0.36)+P(D|C)(0.3) \\ 0.37 & =0.085+0.072+0.3P(D|C) \\ 0.3P(D|C) & =0.213 \\ P(D|C) & =0.71\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected cow from ranch $C$ is a dairy cow is $71%.$
